slot.subtopic: van 't Hoff factor and complexes / isotonic solutions
slot.brief: Compare osmotic pressure of an electrolyte/complex solution with a given dissociation/association degree against a nonelectrolyte; solve for i and then concentration — hard multi-step colligative computation.

stem: At the same temperature, a solution of $\text{[Co(NH}_3\text{)}_5\text{Cl]Cl}_2$ is isotonic with $0.50\ \text{M}$ glucose. The salt dissociates as $\text{[Co(NH}_3\text{)}_5\text{Cl]}^{2+}+2\text{Cl}^-$. If $75\%$ dissociates, what is its concentration?

verdicts.working: For the salt, the van’t Hoff factor is i = 1 + (3 − 1)(0.75) = 2.5. Isotonicity gives 2.5C = 0.50, so C = 0.200 mol L⁻¹.

working:
$i=1+\alpha(\nu-1)=1+0.75(3-1)=2.5$; isotonicity gives $iC=0.50$; $C=\dfrac{0.50}{2.5}=0.200\ \text{mol L}^{-1}$.

Independent check: For the salt, the van’t Hoff factor is i = 1 + (3 − 1)(0.75) = 2.5. Isotonicity gives 2.5C = 0.50, so C = 0.200 mol L⁻¹.
solution: The salt produces $3$ ions on complete dissociation, so $i=1+\alpha(3-1)=1+0.75(2)=2.5$. For isotonic solutions, $iC=0.50$, hence $C=\dfrac{0.50}{2.5}=0.200\ \text{mol L}^{-1}$.
